title: I Took the Oneg Signup Sheet to the Chair Who Never Brought Kugel

parts.text: I signed kugel for week 3 and at 12:12 p.m. the table had a store cake and no kugel. Chair Ruth's name was on my line in different ink. The sheet said: SIGN WHAT YOU BRING. INK MATCHES THE DISH. I was fifty-six, congregant, holding an empty pan slot. Ruth shrugged. "Chairs are the table." I photographed the ink mismatch, the sheet, and the cake. Then I logged a swap. At 12:20 the rabbi's office asked why Ruth's ink was on my kugel line. I asked once, then I documented twice. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The office can see Ruth's different ink on my kugel line next to a store cake.

social.video_title: The chair overwrote my kugel line with a store cake — Part 1/2
social.description: Oneg table, a signup sheet, and mismatched ink. I logged the swap. Would you have photographed the cake?

parts.text: Ruth called it backup until the office asked for the log. I printed the swap, the photo, and the sheet. Kugel returned to the roster. Ruth signed cake as cake and told the kitchen backup was always about optics. Optics is a word chairs use when ink exists. Signup now has a second line: CHAIRS BRING WHAT THEY SIGN. I keep week 3. Ruth bakes or she doesn't. The table finally looks like a sheet, not a rewrite. The room sounds like a room again, not a title. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.

social.video_title: Chairs bring what they sign — Part 2/2
social.description: Swap log, restored kugel line, and a second line. Was backup ever my ink?
